name: agent-builder-main-flow
body:
When a project change-set is in flight and implementation is blocked because the repo's code-writer agents are missing or outdated, some LLMs wrongly refuse — they read the project-flow rule "main is never a mutation place" as forbidding any change on main, including the agent-builder's `.opencode/agents/**` and `opencode.json` edits. In fact code-writer agents are ALWAYS created or updated on the main checkout: the agent-builder's main-write grants are `.opencode/agents/**` and the repo's `opencode.json` agent→model map, resolved against the session workspace root (the main checkout), there is no `apg/.worktrees/*/.opencode/agents/**` mirror, and the running opencode session loads agents from the main checkout / `~/.opencode/agents/`. A created/updated agent therefore can never live on the project branch alone. The required process is:

1. The navigator (codebase-navigator / coordinator) recognises that implementation cannot progress because a code-writer agent must be created or modified.
2. The navigator tasks the `agent-builder` subagent to do the agent work ON THE MAIN CHECKOUT — the only place it has a write grant anyway.
3. The agent-builder scaffolds/updates `.opencode/agents/**` and creates/updates the repo's `opencode.json` agent→model map, AND COMMITS those changes on main.
4. The navigator rebases the project worktree onto main, to stay in sync.
5. The navigator re-scans the worktree.
6. Before implementation continues, the user must restart opencode (to load the new/updated agents and their grants) and reconnect to the session.

The clarification that must be explicit: "main is never a mutation place" governs the binary's GUARDED mutations — durable `apg node`/`apg edge` and transient plan/review mutations, which refuse outside a project worktree — and it does NOT forbid the agent-builder's `.opencode/agents/**` and `opencode.json` file edits and their commit on main. `git push` / `git tag` remain human-approved acts.

The templates must carry both the process AND the grant:
- `opencode-suite/agents/agent-builder.md`: its own frontmatter `bash:` block must grant the read-only git patterns EXACTLY — `git status *`, `git log *`, `git branch --show-current`, `git remote -v`, `git remote show *`, `git ls-files *` — plus `git add *` and `git commit *`. It must NOT grant the blanket `git branch *` or `git remote *`: their option/subcommand surface includes ref-writing forms (`git branch -f <branch> <sha>`, `git branch -D`, `git branch -m`) and config-mutating forms (`git remote add`/`remove`/`set-url`), none of which the agent-builder needs — its only git mutation is `git add` + `git commit`, and push/tag belong to the optional release-agent. It must also state that `git log *` admits the output-redirect option `--output=<file>` (an arbitrary-file write, including inside the main checkout), so `--output=<file>` is FORBIDDEN on every granted git verb — the agent-builder logs to stdout only — a prose-enforced known risk, the glob not being able to exclude the form. Today the block grants the blanket `git branch *` and `git remote *`; this change-set narrows them to the exact read-only patterns above and adds `git add *` and `git commit *`.
- `opencode-suite/agents/codebase-navigator.md`: its "### Codebase agents (delegate — never scaffold or implement yourself)" section (around lines 434-451) must state the escalation — when agents are missing/outdated it tasks the agent-builder on the main checkout, the agent-builder commits there, then the navigator rebases the worktree onto main, re-scans, and the user restarts opencode before implementation continues — and must state that "never mutate main" refers to the binary's node/edge/plan/review mutations, not to this delegation. (The navigator's frontmatter already grants `git rebase *`.)
- `AGENTS.md`: its project-flow section carries the same on-main → commit → rebase-worktree → re-scan → user-restart-opencode flow and the main-mutation clarification.

Acceptance criteria:
- The agent-builder template's frontmatter `bash:` block grants `git add *` and `git commit *` alongside the read-only git patterns, and those read-only patterns are EXACTLY `git status *`, `git log *`, `git branch --show-current`, `git remote -v`, `git remote show *`, `git ls-files *` — the blanket `git branch *` and `git remote *` (which admit ref-writing `git branch -f`/`-D`/`-m` and config-mutating `git remote add`/`remove`/`set-url` forms) are NOT granted; its rule 2 no longer forbids git mutation outright but permits add+commit with push/tag human-approved, and names the read-only git verbs as the narrowed patterns.
- It states that `--output=<file>` is FORBIDDEN on every granted git verb (the `git log *` residue recorded as a known risk).
- The agent-builder template body states that it scaffolds/updates `.opencode/agents/**` AND creates/updates the repo's `opencode.json` agent→model map on the main checkout, and commits there.
- The navigator template's "Codebase agents" section states the escalation and the full on-main → commit → rebase-worktree → re-scan → user-restart-opencode flow, and states that "never mutate main" scopes to the binary's node/edge/plan/review mutations, not to the agent-builder delegation.
- `AGENTS.md` states the same flow and clarification.
- Scope is product source + the repo guide only: `opencode-suite/agents/agent-builder.md`, `opencode-suite/agents/codebase-navigator.md`, `AGENTS.md`. The repo's own `.opencode/agents/**` are consumer artifacts refreshed out-of-band and are NOT edited. This change-set adds NO tests and no binary change.
